prompt: Which eight-legged meadow creature is NOT an insect?
hint: Insects have six legs, but spiders have eight!

fact.text: Spiders are arachnids with eight legs, while every true insect has six legs!

prompt: Which of these forest wonders is NOT a plant?
hint: Mushrooms are fungi, so they cannot make their own food.

fact.text: Mushrooms are fungi, which cannot make food from sunlight like green plants do!

prompt: Tap all the animals that lay eggs in nests or soil!
hint: Look for the turtle with a shell and the soaring eagle.

fact.text: Female turtles bury their eggs in sand or soil to hatch in warmth!

prompt: Tap all the creatures that can flutter through the air!
hint: Butterflies, bees, and even furry bats have wings for flying!

fact.text: Bats are the only mammals on Earth that have wings and can fly!

prompt: Order the stages of a butterfly's life cycle from start!
hint: Start from egg, hatch to caterpillar, form chrysalis, then emerge flying.

fact.text: Inside the chrysalis, a caterpillar transforms completely into a colorful flying butterfly!

prompt: Order how a plant grows from a seed into flower!
hint: Begin with the seed in soil and finish with the bloom.

fact.text: A planted seed sprouts tender roots downward and pushes green leaves toward sunlight!

prompt: Which planet is the hottest planet in our solar system?
hint: Mercury is closest, but Venus traps extreme heat under thick clouds.

fact.text: Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system because its atmosphere traps heat!

prompt: What kind of space object is our bright daytime Sun?
hint: The Sun is not a planet: it is our nearest star.

fact.text: The light of daytime on Earth comes from our closest star, the Sun!

prompt: Tap all the objects that produce their own glowing light!
hint: The Moon does not make light: it reflects light from the Sun!

fact.text: The Moon does not make light; it simply reflects light from the Sun!

prompt: Tap all the giant planets that have rings around them!
hint: Saturn has famous rings, but Jupiter and Uranus have rings too!

fact.text: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune all have rings circling around them in space!

prompt: Order the first four rocky planets starting closest to Sun!
hint: Start at Mercury, then Venus, our Earth, and red planet Mars.

fact.text: Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars are the four rocky planets closest to the Sun!

prompt: Order these space neighbors from closest to Earth to furthest!
hint: The Moon orbits Earth, Sun is next, distant stars are furthest.

fact.text: The Moon is our closest space neighbor, completing an orbit around Earth monthly!

prompt: Who has MORE bones inside their human skeleton right now?
hint: Babies start with about 300 bones that fuse together over time!

fact.text: Babies are born with about 300 bones, which fuse into 206 adult bones!

prompt: Which is the LARGEST single organ of the human body?
hint: It covers your body from your head all the way to your toes!

fact.text: Skin is the largest organ of the human body, shielding our internal muscles!

prompt: Tap all the objects that float upon the water's surface!
hint: Wood and apples float, and bubbly volcanic pumice rock floats too!

fact.text: Pumice is a volcanic rock full of gas holes that actually floats on water!

prompt: Tap all the sensory parts found on your smiling face!
hint: Knees bend for running, but eyes, nose, and tongue explore senses!

fact.text: Your tongue has taste buds that detect sweet, salty, sour, and bitter flavors!

prompt: Order these human growth stages from youngest to oldest age!
hint: Start in the cradle as an infant and grow into adulthood.

fact.text: Humans grow fastest during infancy, often doubling their size in early years!

prompt: Order what happens as healthy food journeys through your body!
hint: Teeth chew first, throat swallows, and stomach digests into energy.

fact.text: Your stomach churns food with digestive juices to fuel your active muscles!
